name: Fred Hampton
role: Deputy chairman of the Black Panther Party and chairman of its Illinois chapter (1968-1969)
summary: Hampton was a Marxist-Leninist revolutionary who argued that the Black struggle is a class struggle, that racism is a by-product of capitalism, and that a vanguard party must educate and arm the people. He built a multiracial Rainbow Coalition and free community programs while advocating armed self-defence against the police and rejecting cultural nationalism and black capitalism.

limit-guns.rationale: Said there was nothing wrong with guns in the community, only a misdistribution because the police hold them all, and that Black people needed to arm themselves.

empower-police-military.rationale: Denounced the police as fascist 'pigs' who occupy communities like a foreign territory and campaigned to decentralise them.

gradual-change.rationale: Said the party stood for 'the complete revolution' and would not 'half do a thing'; rejected petitioning authorities as a cycle of futility.

revolution-justified.rationale: Called for 'international proletarian revolution' and said he hoped to die as a revolutionary; described revolution as the cure for a 'sick society'.

one-party-rule.rationale: Described the vanguard party leading the people after the social revolution until they are educated enough to run things; also called for a 'People's Party' ticket.

political-violence-never.rationale: Said it was no longer a question of violence or nonviolence but of resistance to fascism, and that war is abolished only through war.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Said revolution is always a class struggle (citing Marx, Lenin, Mao, Che) and that the priority of the struggle is class, with racism a by-product of capitalism.

direct-action.rationale: Inferred: stressed learning through 'observation and participation' and acting over writing, while also backing a People's Party ticket, so evidence on elections versus direct action is mixed.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Described the free breakfast and free clinic as open to anyone whose only qualification is being hungry or sick.

production-for-use.rationale: Judged programs by whether they meet the needs of the masses, described the Breakfast for Children program as running 'in a socialistic manner', and attacked businesses that profit from the community.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Said anyone who comes into the community to make profit off the people by exploiting them is a capitalist and must be driven out.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rejected 'the dictatorship of the Panthers' or of Black people but said 'We are for the dictatorship of the people', with the vanguard educating the people after the revolution until they run things themselves.

national-self-determination.rationale: Backed the Vietnamese people's right to self-determination and called for victory for Vietnam against US forces.

class-collaboration.rationale: Held that employers (capitalists, 'avaricious greedy businessmen') and the oppressed are opposed classes; argued capitalists, black or white, must be driven out of the community.

workers-nation.rationale: Said the way to fight reactionaries is 'international proletarian revolution' and described a coalition of black, white, brown and yellow masses.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Said the party was not a racist organisation, would fight racism with solidarity, and denounced Judge Taney's ruling that Black people have no rights.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Described the oppressor as a 'three-in-one' of greedy businessmen, lying politicians and fascist police, and said the legal system was set up to keep the money-makers' arrangements going.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Called politicians 'demagogic, lyin'' and said Democrats and Republicans sell out their voters and independents sell to the highest bidder.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Said police who step outside legality should be arrested (a 'citizens' arrest' demonstration) and denounced police killings of young Black residents as murder.

vanguard-party.rationale: Repeatedly asserted that the Black Panther Party is the vanguard party and that the people follow and are educated by the vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Said the masses are poor and that any program brought into a community should be analysed to see that it meets that community's needs; led programs feeding hungry children and offering free health care.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Mocked people with 'more degrees than a thermometer' who lack practice and students who think they serve the struggle by talking.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Described himself as a dialectical materialist and argued that the economic motive of capitalism came first and racism followed from it as a by-product.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Contested: held up Newton and the vanguard setting an armed example, yet called the Weathermen's confrontations premature, adventurist and on the brink of anarchism because the people were not ready.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: said the established press and ruling interests 'talked us into believing' we were nobody and called papers 'ideological servants' of fascism.

informal-organisation.rationale: Insisted on a disciplined vanguard party with six weeks of political education for members and attacked spontaneous, anarchistic groups as leading people to massacre.

defeat-communism.rationale: Welcomed the label communist, said the people 'can call it communism' and it would not scare anybody, and cited China as a model of people running things.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Self-described Marxist-Leninist who said 'you fight capitalism with socialism' and denied communism is something to fear.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Said people should take over control of their communities, that programs should be analysed by the people they serve, and that the community would run the breakfast and health programs.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Insisted on armed self-defence and retaliation, saying the party would 'blow their brains out' if police attacked, and that attacks must be met reciprocally.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Contested: held that the struggle is class not race and built a multiracial coalition, but also ran a Black-led party and said 'Black Power to Black People' alongside power to every other group.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Called for arming the people and for equal distribution of guns, rejecting police monopoly on arms.

workers-own-party.rationale: Said Democrat, Republican and Independent labels all mean selling out and that he wanted candidates running on a 'People's Party'.

notes: Died in 1969 aged 21, so the record is a single year of speeches. The Black Panther Party's Ten-Point Program was not used unless he championed a point in his own words. The Weathermen criticism and the call to decentralise the police come from recorded interviews.
